This pattern is primarily a web concern. 4. 5. ## Principles 6. 7. - The structure of the view is exposed via platform semantics (regions/landmarks). 8. - One top-level heading describes the view topic. 9. - Users can bypass repeated navigation blocks to reach the main content. 10. - Each navigable region is distinguishable by name when more than one exists. 11. - Interactive cards / tiles have exactly one primary activation target; secondary actions inside a card don't nest interactive controls. 12. - Promotional / dismissible surfaces have named controls. 13. - Respect user motion / color-scheme preferences. 14. 15. ## Web implementation 16. 17. ### General defaults 18. 19. - **Landmarks**: `
`, `
`, `
`, `
` used for their semantic roles. Exactly one `
`. 20. - **Skip link**: first focusable element; targets `#maincontent` on `
`. See `references/keyboard-focus.md`. 21. - **Headings**: one `

`, typically in the hero or the start of `
`; section `

`s; no skipped levels. 22. - **Page title**: descriptive ``. 23. - **Multiple `<nav>`**: each has a unique accessible name (`aria-label="Primary"`, `aria-label="Footer"`, `aria-label="Breadcrumb"`). 24. - **Product cards / listings**: wrap the primary link around the product name (or use a block-scoped link pattern). Don't put a `<button>` inside an `<a>` or an `<a>` inside a `<button>`. If the card has both a link and action buttons (Add to cart, Save), keep them as siblings in the DOM with a clear visual and programmatic separation.
